testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which one do you NOT have to show?

options.text: The oil pressure gauge is working.
The oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal oil pressure.
The oil temperature gauge rises to normal operating temperature.
The oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during inspection, make sure it works. The gauge should show normal oil pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If your vehicle has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: How should you hold a steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands. Position your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until all construction is done.

questions.explanation: In work zones, drive at posted speed limits. Reduce your speed even more when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles (like reflective triangles).

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which one will you NOT have to do?

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: To get your CDL, you must pass a vehicle inspection test. You will walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each item, and explain what you are checking and why. You will not crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

questions.question: What does Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) mean?

options.text: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.
The total weight of the vehicle without any load.
The total weight of cargo minus the containers.
The maximum weight allowed to be transported.

questions.correctAnswerText: The loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the loaded weight of a single vehicle as given by the manufacturer.

questions.question: If a cargo cover flaps while you drive, what could happen?
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind while driving. A flapping cover can tear loose, uncover your cargo, and block your view or others' views.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror.
Only use the passenger's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors often when backing to watch for hazards behind your vehicle. Use a helper to watch blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: If a traffic light has been green for a long time, what is likely to happen?

options.text: It will stay green as you approach.
It will soon change to yellow.
It will skip yellow and go straight to red.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will soon change to yellow.
questions.explanation: If a traffic light has been green for a long time as you approach, it will likely turn yellow soon. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until all construction is done.

questions.explanation: In work zones, reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: In a convex mirror, objects appear ____ than they really are.
questions.explanation: A convex mirror makes objects look smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Pull forward into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice that forms on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. The road shows through it, making the road look wet instead of icy.

questions.question: When starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:
questions.explanation: After starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, listen for unusual noises.

questions.question: The maximum speed limit in a residential area, unless otherwise posted, is:
questions.explanation: Unless a different speed limit is posted, the maximum speed limit in residential or business areas is 25 mph. Always follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: Failing to exit your vehicle properly during the basic vehicle control skills test will result in:

options.text: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
An extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face it and keep three points of contact at all times. For buses, hold the handrail. Exiting improperly results in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: A vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) uses a ____ light to warn that the system is not working properly.
questions.explanation: ABS warning lights are usually yellow. If the ABS is not working, you can still use your regular brakes.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, you should make sure that:

options.text: The pedal surface has been smoothed out.
There is something underneath the brake pedal.

questions.explanation: Check that nothing under or around the pedals blocks them from working. Make sure the pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces.

questions.question: While operating a CMV:

options.text: You are not required to wear a safety belt.
You are only required to wear a safety belt if your vehicle does not have airbags.
You are required to wear a safety belt only if hauling more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You are always required to wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are always required to wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection during a collision. You must always wear a safety belt when operating a CMV.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check tire inflation?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire inflation during a vehicle inspection test. Kicking the tires does not count as a passing inspection.

questions.question: What is the only way to become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up—not coffee, cold showers, or exercise. The only way to sober up is to wait.

questions.question: To make night driving easier, you should:

options.text: Make your instrument panel lights as dim as possible while still reading the gauges.
Not take a nap before driving.
Use only your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make your instrument panel lights as dim as possible while still reading the gauges.
questions.explanation: Bright interior lights make it harder to see outside at night. Keep the interior light off and set your instrument lights to the lowest level that lets you read the gauges clearly.

questions.question: Mismatched tire sizes:

options.text: Can only be used on a front axle.
Can only be used on a trailer's axles.
Must be fixed before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be fixed before you drive.
questions.explanation: All tires on your vehicle should be the same size. Check that your tires match when you inspect your vehicle.

questions.question: When inspecting your vehicle's exhaust system, which is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are leaking
Exhaust system parts made of aluminum

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts made of aluminum
questions.explanation: Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing pipes and mufflers; loose or missing brackets and bolts; parts rubbing against fuel system parts; and leaks. The material used (like aluminum) is not a concern.

questions.question: During your on-road driving test, you must do everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely and responsibly at all times during the test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals even when no other cars are present, following all traffic laws, and avoiding accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done.
Can only be done in dry weather.

questions.explanation: Blocking your cargo prevents it from sliding during transport. When cargo shifts, it makes steering and handling much harder for the driver.

questions.question: A suspension system:

options.text: Has a maximum weight capacity rating.
Uses pressurized water to support the load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has a maximum weight capacity rating.
questions.explanation: Manufacturers give suspension systems a maximum weight capacity rating that cannot be exceeded.

questions.question: When parked on the side of a road, you should:

options.text: Stand in the roadway and wave your arms.

questions.explanation: Use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be lifted with a jack.

questions.explanation: The engine may need to be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive below the posted speed limit.
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. You must constantly adjust your speed to match the current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When making tight maneuvers, what should you do?

options.text: Open your door for a better view.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when driving in tight spaces.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release it. If it doesn't return to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release it. If you hear a squeak, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when the brake pedal is pressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the brake pedal three times. Then press and hold the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other problem.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable?

options.text: Dual tires that do not touch each other.
Tires of different sizes if used only on short trips.
Retreaded tires on the front of a school bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual tires that do not touch each other.
questions.explanation: Dual tires must not touch each other or other parts of the vehicle. Tire sizes must match. Do not use cracked or damaged tires. Retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: How many points on your record will result in a suspended license?
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, driving violations add points to your record. If you get 12 or more points, your license will be suspended.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Do not wear gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Wear gloves or use a cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly near road workers.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: What can affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your vehicle's speed, its weight, and how much grip the road surface provides.

questions.question: What is true about over-the-counter medication?

options.text: It poses no safety risks to drivers.
Laws do not mention it regarding impaired driving.
It cannot affect a driver's ability.
It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect a person's ability to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter and prescription medications can have side effects that make driving unsafe. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any controlled substance, including some over-the-counter medications.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you that you may slow down?
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes to make the brake lights flash. This lets drivers behind you know you are slowing down.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you lose points by:

options.text: Exiting the vehicle one time to check your positioning.

questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses an exercise boundary line. Each time you cross a line, you lose points on your skills test score.

questions.question: In cold weather, an alcohol evaporator should be checked and filled:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in an air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by one-half or more on packed snow. Stopping and turning are difficult on slippery surfaces, so you must drive slower for safety.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing:

options.text: Do not rely only on warning signals.
Roll down your window to listen for a train.
Only check the track closest to your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals.
questions.explanation: Never depend only on warning signals to alert you to a train. Never try to beat a train across the tracks. If there are multiple tracks, check all tracks in both directions before crossing.

questions.question: Where can you find the tire load rating?

options.text: On the inside of the driver's door
On the side of each tire

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of each tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry. This number is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: For safety, when should you turn off a retarder?

options.text: When you are carrying a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces braking. But it can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn it off in wet, snowy, or icy conditions.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: You should always use at least ____ to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, even small items, must have a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the road, move out of the lane next to it if you can. If you cannot move safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Header boards:

options.text: Protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
Protect the driver's head when entering the cab of a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called "headache racks," protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.
